findings.title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author link
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch now uses 70% instead of 30%, so the link is much lighter and has poor contrast on light themes. This is a regression for the default theme, and it is inconsistent with the PR's stated aim of only adding dark-theme handling. The light branch should stay at 30%, with a 70% secondary branch for dark themes.

findings.title: Group member name light color silently changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value therefore changes from 30% to 50%, which lightens the name and makes it look the same as the title. The light branch should remain 30%, with the dark branch at 70%.

findings.title: Mobile group member name light color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, so the light-theme appearance changes unintentionally. The light branch should keep 30%, paired with `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for dark themes.

findings.title: Topic map h3 light color changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light theme gets a much lighter heading, and the heading now looks the same as the h4. The intended pair is 20% for light and 80% for dark, matching the other `.number, i` rule.

findings.title: Custom message length light color changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, so light-theme text becomes much darker. The desktop equivalent correctly uses 70%/30%. The pair here should be `$primary` 70% and `$secondary` 30%.
